answer: Each agent identity must periodically complete a unique sequential computation bound to its own key, a puzzle that cannot be split across machines or reused by clones. Like a fable where a willow bends but never breaks under load, the wharf of the economy only admits identities that keep proving real compute time. A sybil farm running ten thousand fake agents must solve ten thousand separate puzzles, so its cost grows linearly with every fake, while an honest agent pays just one.
